author: Ranjith Shivahari

definitions.meaning: A person shows willingness to do or not do something, to get the other party's assent. Acceptance of it makes a promise.
definitions.note: Intention to be bound is the test

definitions.meaning: A step that only invites others to make an offer. It does not bind the person who invites.
definitions.note: Acceptance of it makes no contract

doubt.question: Goods with a price tag in a shop window: is that an offer?
doubt.answer: No. It is an invitation to offer. The customer offers to buy at the counter, and the shopkeeper may accept or refuse.

exam_tip: In an MCQ, look for the words price list, catalogue, tender notice or auction announcement. They point to an invitation to offer.

insight.punchline: Display invites, bid or buyer offers!
insight.text: In an invitation, the other side makes the offer and the inviter decides whether to accept it.

key_points: Offer + ==acceptance== = agreement. Invitation + offer = still no agreement until accepted.
Price tags, price lists, catalogues and ==tender notices== are invitations to offer.
At an auction, the announcement invites offers. The ==bid is the offer==, accepted by fall of hammer.
An advertisement promising a reward to anyone who performs a condition is a ==general offer== (Carlill case).

memory_trick.explanation: A display or notice only opens the door for customers. The bid, the bell the customer rings, is the real offer. The reward advertisement is the exception: it is an offer.

mistakes.wrong: A tender notice is an offer, so bidders can sue on it
mistakes.right: A tender notice is an invitation. The bidder's tender is the offer, and the contract forms when it is accepted.

mistakes.wrong: Every advertisement is only an invitation to offer
mistakes.right: An advertisement promising a reward for a condition is a general offer, as in Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.

mistakes.wrong: The auctioneer's announcement is the offer; the bid is acceptance
mistakes.right: The announcement invites offers. The bidder makes the offer and the auctioneer accepts it by fall of hammer.

mistakes.wrong: A shopkeeper must sell goods once the price tag is shown
mistakes.right: The tag is an invitation. The shopkeeper can refuse the customer's offer to buy.

mistakes_hook: don't fall for the ad trap!

simple_words: An offer can be accepted to make a contract. An invitation only asks people to come forward with offers.
steps: Find who shows willingness to be bound
Check for a price list, catalogue or tender
If yes, it is an invitation to offer
Find the other side's offer, then acceptance
Check for a reward ad (general offer)

Checker 1: Table row 2, Offer column: 'Acceptance makes a contract' is loose wording. Under Section 2(b), an accepted proposal becomes a promise, and under Section 2(e) it becomes an agreement. It is a contract only if the Section 10 essentials are also met. Correct version: 'Acceptance makes a promise or agreement (a contract if the other essentials are met)'. This also keeps it consistent with key point 1.

Checker 1: Mistake 1 right: 'the contract forms when it is accepted' has the same looseness. Better: 'the agreement (and so the contract, if the other essentials are met) forms when the tender is accepted.'
